newsitem.title: USA: TCF Financial Q1 net interest income up.
newsitem.headline: TCF Financial Q1 net interest income up.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Tuesday its first quarter net interest income was a record $86 million, up from $84.5 million for the 1996 quarter.
Earlier, TCF reported first quarter income of $0.83 a sahre, up from $0.73 a year ago.

"Our first-quarter results were highlighted by record net interest income and a 17 percent increase in fee income over last year," TCF Chairman William Cooper said in a statement. "We achieved this improvement primarily by growing higher-yielding consumer and commercial loans and lower interest-cost retail deposit accounts."
First quarter fee and service charge revenues for the quarter rose to $25.6 million from $22.6 million.
Non-interest income, excluding 1996 bank branch and related loan sale gains, totaled $40.4 million for the 1997 first quarter, compared with $34.6 million for the 1996 first quarter.
Non-performing assets, which was principally real estate acquired through foreclosure and non-accrual loans, amounted to $44.9 million at March 31, down from $46.2 million at December 31, 1996.

TCF said it provided $1.1 million for credit losses in the 1997 first quarter, down from $2.8 million in the 1996 first quarter. Net loan chargeoffs were $2.1 million in the 1997 first quarter, compared with $1.9 million in the same 1996 period.
TCF is a $7 billion bank holding company based in Minneapolis.
